newsitem.title: USA: CBOT March soybeans hit 4-month high on USDA data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT March soybeans hit 4-month high on USDA data.

text.p: CBOT soybeans ended Wednesday's session with double-digit gains and the March contract touched a four-month high after USDA trimmed ending stocks estimates in its supply and demand data, traders said.
"There was big volume and it was very impressive. We have a tightening carryover for beans," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter in describing action in the soybean pit.

The data, released Wednesday, indicated U.S. ending stocks would fall to 140 million bushels, 15 million less than the USDA predicted in January. Traders had expected a cut but there had been speculation USDA would be more conservative.
The report also showed an increase in crushing rates by 10 million bushels to 1.410 billion. USDA bumped export demand by five million to 905 million bushels.
Those increases were offset by gains in soybean production estimates for Brazil and Argentina.
Brazil was forecast to harvest 26.50 million tonnes, up 0.05 million from the previous report. Argentina's production estimate was raised by 0.5 million tonnes to 13.50 million.
March soybeans peaked at $7.65-1/2 per bushel, the highest since October 2 when that contract touched $7.75. Other months closed 14-1/2 to two cents per bushel higher.
Commercials were noted sellers on the day with Cargill Inc, Farmers Commodities Corp and Produce Grain the largest sellers, traders said. Continental Grain spread two million bushels July/November.

Prudential Securities bought four million bushels March and 3.5 million May, Tenco Inc bought four million March and two million May and Refco Inc bought 3.5 million March and two million May, traders said.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock bought 1,300 May $7.25 puts at 8-1/2 to 8-1/4 cents. Cargill Investor Services bought 500 March $7.25 puts at one cent and 500 May $7.50 puts at 20 cents, traders said.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 65,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume 47,661 contracts.
